key_insight: Brain2Vec learns reusable 3D brain MRI representations that improve brain-age prediction and support downstream classification.
clinical_relevance: The model could reduce labeled-data and computing requirements for structural brain MRI research, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Self-supervised pretraining on 74,425 T1-weighted MRI scans pooled from multiple studies.
Use pretrained weights for task-specific fine-tuning or frozen embeddings as standalone features.
Assess predictive performance, convergence speed, and anatomical interpretability.
evidence_signal: Pretrained initialization improved brain-age accuracy and convergence versus random initialization; frozen embeddings outperformed anatomical volume features on four of five classification tasks.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish prospective clinical performance or generalizability across deployment settings.
paper_title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
